sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (match the columns, true/false, fill in the blanks or one-word answers).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Teachers have to manage a classroom full of children with diverse needs and ________. (ii) An unconditional love and care helps in developing a sense of ________ between children and teachers.
Fill in the blanks: (i) ECCE teachers should use ________ low-cost and no-cost material. (ii) ________ and systematic planning helps in attaining the desired outcomes.
State True or False: (i) Being organised helps teachers conduct activities smoothly. (ii) Regular communication between parents and teachers is not needed in ECCE.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False — it helps understand children's needs and developmental stages.

questions.q: Match: (a) Empathetic listener (b) Effective communicator — (i) Uses gestures, postures and voice modulation in storytelling (ii) Understands children's thoughts and emotions (iii) Uses only costly materials

Answer in one word: (i) The quality of a teacher who keeps learning new knowledge and skills throughout the career. (ii) The quality that helps a teacher repeat the same thing several times for a child without getting upset.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What quality should ECCE teachers possess to conduct activities smoothly?
questions.answer: They should be organised: ECCE teachers have to organise the classroom, create teaching-learning materials, design bulletin boards and conduct parent-teacher meetings, so being organised lets all activities run smoothly.

or.q: Why are communication skills important for ECCE teachers?
or.answer: Teachers must communicate with children, parents, the principal and community. Clear, simple language with gestures, postures and voice modulation engages young children in stories, rhymes and role play and sustains interest; it also builds rapport with parents and stakeholders.

questions.q: How does being loving and caring contribute to children's development in an ECCE setting?
questions.answer: Unconditional love and care develop trust between children and teachers, help children settle in a new space and support sound social and emotional development. Concern for each child's needs forms a lasting bond, gives a sense of belonging and helps solve classroom problems through mutual understanding.

questions.q: What role do ECCE teachers play in building rapport with parents and the community?
questions.answer: They keep regular communication with parents to understand children's needs and developmental stages, value the role of parents, and encourage parents and community members to take part in the centre, which reduces the gap between home and centre and supports optimum development.

questions.q: Briefly state the roles and responsibilities of an ECCE teacher.
questions.answer: Ensuring children's physical and emotional safety; planning curriculum, timetable and activities; designing and implementing the curriculum; creating an enriching environment with suitable materials; addressing diversity and supporting children with disabilities; regular assessment; organising parent-teacher meetings, special talks and events.

questions.q: Why should an ECCE teacher be patient and persistent?
questions.answer: Children may misplace toys, mess up the room or not learn in the expected way; one child may need things repeated several times and another special attention. A patient, persistent teacher does not get angry, gives freedom to explore safely and keeps working for positive outcomes.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What makes an ECCE teacher effective? Describe three qualities with examples from the classroom.
questions.answer: Any three, e.g.: Loving and caring — unconditional love builds trust and belonging and helps socio-emotional development. Active and empathetic listener — understands children's thoughts and feelings and solves behaviour problems. Patient and persistent — repeats and supports without anger. Flexible and adjusting — works with limited resources and diverse needs. Creative and innovative — nurtures curiosity and new ideas. Effective communicator — clear, simple language and good rapport with parents. Well trained and a lifelong learner.
questions.note: October 2021 asked: what are the qualities of an effective ECCE teacher?

questions.q: How can ECCE teachers create an enriched learning environment for children?
questions.answer: By organising the classroom — space for different activities, age-appropriate equipment, space suited to children with disabilities, safety; using varied teaching-learning materials, including locally available low-cost and no-cost materials recycled creatively (cartons, bottles, pebbles, leaves); planning age- and developmentally appropriate activities to play, observe, manipulate, explore and experiment; making every child feel respected, accepted and welcome; and assessing regularly through observation, anecdotal records and portfolios.

questions.q: Describe the role of an ECCE teacher in organising programmes and events.
questions.answer: Scheduling and organising parent-teacher meetings so parents and teachers work together for children's development; arranging special talks and interactions on everyday topics such as safe drinking water, saving water and electricity, planting trees, healthy food and protecting animals; celebrating special days with active participation of children; and conducting orientation programmes and workshops for parents and community members.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Discuss any four qualities of an ECCE teacher.
questions.answer: (1) Loving and caring: children entering a new space need an affectionate teacher; unconditional love builds trust, a lasting bond and a sense of belonging, and supports social and emotional development. (2) Active and empathetic listener: empathy — putting oneself in the child's shoes — helps the teacher recognise children's thoughts and emotions and solve classroom and behaviour problems. (3) Patient and persistent: children may make a mess or need repetition and special attention; the teacher stays calm and keeps striving for positive outcomes while giving freedom to explore safely. (4) Creative and innovative: nurtures children's curiosity and novel ways of thinking by giving chances to experiment. Others: energetic and motivated, cheerful and committed, flexible, organised, effective communicator, good rapport with parents, self-confident, well trained, lifelong learner with research skills.

questions.q: What are the roles and responsibilities of ECCE teachers in planning activities and creating an enriching teaching-learning environment?
questions.answer: Planning: the teacher plans the curriculum, timetable, age-appropriate indoor and outdoor activities, assessment procedures, parent-teacher meetings and workshops, keeping in mind children's needs, society's expectations and the resources available; planning must be thoughtful and systematic. She also helps design and implement the curriculum. Enriching environment: organise and manage the classroom — allocate space for different activities, select age-appropriate equipment and materials, arrange space for children with disabilities and ensure safety; use a variety of teaching-learning materials, including locally available low-cost and no-cost materials and recycled objects, used in many ways (pebbles for counting and textures); organise developmentally appropriate experiences such as role play and park visits; ensure that every child feels respected, accepted and welcomed; and assess regularly through observation, anecdotal records and portfolios.
